MD5.title: MD5 Hashing
MD5.description: MD5 is a cryptographically broken hashing algorithm and should not be used for security-sensitive applications.
MD5.recommendation: Use SHA-256, SHA-3, or another modern cryptographic hash.

SHA-1.title: SHA-1 Hashing
SHA-1.description: SHA-1 is considered cryptographically weak for new security-sensitive applications.
SHA-1.recommendation: Use SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, or SHA-3.

DES.title: DES Encryption
DES.description: DES has an insufficient effective security level and is considered obsolete.

3DES.title: 3DES Encryption
3DES.description: 3DES is an older encryption algorithm that is unsuitable for many new applications.

AES-ECB.title: AES-ECB Mode
AES-ECB.description: ECB mode can reveal patterns because identical plaintext blocks can produce identical ciphertext blocks.
AES-ECB.recommendation: Use an authenticated encryption mode such as AES-GCM where appropriate.
